scope: All canonical T07-T11 criterion and delayed task texts searched for the actual named runtime/format obligations; broad gap prose is interpreted against these concrete contracts

assignments.task: For a synthetic PT_LOAD with offset0x1000, vaddr0x400000, filesz0x30, memsz0x50, derive mapped initialized and zero-fill ranges. Compare with a real original ELF and its section-to-segment mapping.

variants.task: Remove the section table from an otherwise supported original executable and explain which loader facts remain available.

assignments.task: Compile the same address-taking source as non-PIE, PIE and shared PIC with consistent compile/link options. Compare runtime-relocation obligations and loaded-address assumptions without treating ET_DYN as sufficient evidence.

variants.task: Build a supported static-PIE variant and locate its self-relocation owner rather than assuming no loader means no relocations.

assignments.task: Load a trusted original plugin by absolute path and then by a controlled local search path; record its recursive dependencies and selected interpreter. Deliberately supply a missing dependency without altering system loader configuration.

variants.task: Relocate the plugin and its dependency together and justify an origin-relative policy without private build paths.

assignments.task: Extend the existing TLS test to record values and addresses for main and two threads before/after independent increments; inspect TLS sections and access sequences. Do not retain a pointer after its thread's lifetime.

variants.task: Load an original TLS-bearing plugin after threads already exist and identify additional loader/runtime responsibilities.

assignments.task: Draw producer/consumer/lifetime chains for TLS templates, init arrays and fini arrays using the supplied runtime source passages and actual metadata. Mark uninspected runtime bodies explicitly instead of filling gaps from function names.

variants.task: Retain only one initialization service in a custom runtime and specify all dependencies its callback contract permits.

assignments.task: Define original sparse bytes at0x1000:{01,02} and0x1010:{FE,FF}; derive raw output under explicit zero-gap fill and an address-bearing Intel HEX output. Decode both independently before any use.

variants.task: Use a nonzero gap-fill byte and show how checksum and image size accounting change.

assignments.task: Produce a stripped original executable and separate debug companion, record hashes/build identity, and resolve one symbol/address through the matching companion. Deliberately pair a different build's debug file and reject it.

variants.task: Re-link identical source at a changed base and explain why the old address correlation fails.

assignments.task: Assign mapping, zero-fill, interpreter loading, symbol relocation, TLS setup and main invocation to kernel, loader or runtime using inspected evidence. Mark any uninspected implementation step explicitly.

variants.task: Remove the dynamic loader from an original image and identify which retained services must now initialize themselves.

assignments.task: Trace inspected musl __init_libc through environment/auxv processing, TLS/stack-protector initialization and stage2 init hooks/main. Contrast with the bounded glibc entry-prefix evidence and label unavailable deeper glibc steps.

variants.task: Retain thread-local errno in a custom-entry proposal and enumerate the additional implementation evidence required before execution.

assignments.task: Define an original custom runtime supporting only argument decoding, bounded byte output and explicit exit. Produce a service table refusing malloc, stdio streams, TLS and constructors unless separately implemented; compile a forbidden-call negative control.

variants.task: Add one initialization hook with a restricted callback contract and show its dependency closure separately.

assignments.task: Build supported dynamic, static and static-PIE versions of one original output program; inventory interpreter, needed libraries, relocations and startup origins. Report unavailable toolchain modes as gaps.

variants.task: Add TLS and identify which previously sufficient minimal startup assumptions no longer hold.

assignments.task: Use an entry breakpoint on the original custom image before any C helper. Record original rsp, entry PC, code bytes and first handoff; diagnose a deliberately wrong saved-stack pointer through inspection.

variants.task: Strip the runtime image and use its hash-matched debug companion to recover the same entry analysis.

assignments.task: Select one observed compiler-rt/libgcc helper, inspect its target-specific declaration/implementation contract, and compare argument/result ABI and exceptional inputs with the learner primitive. Record unavailable source as a gap rather than inventing equivalence.

variants.task: Port the helper interface to a target that returns a value in multiple registers and redo the ABI proof.

assignments.task: Choose a concrete embedded library version and list every required environment service for a tiny formatted-output proposal. Distinguish documented retarget hooks from uninspected implementation dependencies and refuse claims until source/objects are available.

variants.task: Replace formatted output with a bounded raw-byte service and identify which environment obligations disappear and which remain.

assignments.task: Define which owner creates TLS and walks initialization hooks in a custom runtime; provide one original hook that requires a ready service and reject a schedule invoking it too early. Do not borrow hosted TLS implicitly.

variants.task: Add multiple tasks and define separate TLS instance lifetime, initialization and reclamation responsibilities.

conclusion: Tasks require bounded selected implementation contracts, explicit uninspected callees, one compiler-rt/libgcc helper and one concrete embedded output library; they do not require proving every implementation branch of entire libc/compiler libraries. No assigned missing body is closed by its function name.
